backward_compat_traps.rule: A Gen5 device trains at 2.5 GT/s first, then negotiates Recovery up to the highest common rate.
backward_compat_traps.trap: On a Gen4/Gen3 link a Gen5 device silently falls back; the 32.0 GT/s bit is honored only if BOTH ends advertise it.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Gen5 modulation is NRZ (two-level); PAM4 is a Gen6 feature.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming a 32 GT/s PCIe link is PAM4 is wrong; channel budgeting that assumes PAM4 SNR is incorrect for Gen5.

backward_compat_traps.rule: 32 GT/s requires the four-phase enhanced equalization to open the eye before sustaining 32 GT/s.
backward_compat_traps.trap: If EQ fails to converge the link silently drops to a lower rate — lower-than-expected bandwidth with no hard error.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Up to TWO retimers per link; each must participate in the Phase 0-3 handshake.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A third retimer, or one that omits the EQ handshake, breaks 32 GT/s training.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Lane Margining at the Receiver is MANDATORY at Gen5.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Software written for PCIe 1.0-3.0 may misparse the capability list of a Gen5 device that includes the Lane Margining Extended Capability.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Alternate Protocol Negotiation lets a link run CXL over the PCIe 5.0 PHY.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A device advertising Alternate Protocol but implementing only base PCIe must reject the negotiation cleanly.

previous_versions: PCI Express Base Specification 4.0 (2017) — 16 GT/s, 128b/130b, up to two retimers

key_changes.summary: Doubles the per-lane signaling rate to 32 GT/s (NRZ); retains 128b/130b from Gen3/Gen4; adds four-phase enhanced transmitter equalization with preset hints (P0-P10); adds optional transmitter precoding; mandates Lane Margining at the Receiver; carries up to two retimers per link; defines Alternate Protocol Negotiation (used by CXL); keeps the TLP/DLLP/LTSSM/credit-flow-control semantics of base PCIe.

future_versions_industry_outline.summary: Switches NRZ to PAM4, adds FEC, makes FLIT framing mandatory.

fields.version_naming_history_note: PCI-SIG maintains the PCI Express Base Specification. PCIe 5.0 (Rev 5.0, 2019) doubles Gen4 to 32 GT/s while staying on NRZ + 128b/130b. The modulation change to PAM4 + FEC + Flit arrives at PCIe 6.0. The Rev 5.0 base spec is membership-gated; Gen5 facts here are from the public PCI-SIG Rev 5.0 announcement, PCI-SIG briefs, and vendor IP-controller datasheets (Synopsys DesignWare, Cadence, Rambus, PLDA).
